title: Khalsa Sovereignty Is Declared and Kapoor Singh Is Noticed

blocks.text: Darbara Singh’s refusal becomes a wider Panthic argument on this page. The Singhs say that Satguru had conferred sovereignty on the Khalsa Panth, so it would be shameful to trade that divine grant for a title dependent on imperial favor and revocable at a ruler’s whim.

The argument widens from one office to the whole political relationship with the Mughals. The Khalsa will not exchange its future for a lesser arrangement, because Guru-given authority reaches wherever the Panth stands firm and cannot be reduced to a borrowed dignity.

As the debate turns from refusal to selection, attention settles on Kapoor Singh. He is serving the congregation with humility, and a fresh scar that visibly testifies to his courage helps mark him as a Singh whose honor has already been proven in the field.
